subject: Coffee & Tea
title: What Is Specialty Coffee?
description: A short lesson to help you apply What Is Specialty Coffee?.

hook.text: Specialty coffee scores 80+ points on a 100-point scale judged by certified Q-graders. It's the top 5–10% of all coffee.

buildup.text: Scoring evaluates aroma, flavor, aftertaste, acidity, body, balance, and defects. It's rigorous and standardized.

discovery.text: Specialty beans fetch $3–25+ per pound versus $1–2 for commercial grade. Quality commands real premiums.

twist.text: The specialty segment grows 20% annually while total coffee consumption grows only 2%. It's the industry's bright spot.

climax.text: For farmers, producing specialty-grade coffee is the clearest path out of commodity poverty—if they can access training.

punchline.text: Quality scores above 80 unlock a different economy entirely.

quiz.question: What score must coffee achieve to be classified as 'specialty'?

details.summary: Specialty coffee is arabica scoring 80 or above on a 100-point scale evaluated by certified graders. It represents the top 5 to 10 percent of global production. The specialty segment values traceability, quality, and origin character, and commands significant price premiums over commodity coffee.
details.whyItMatters: The specialty coffee movement has driven quality improvements worldwide and created markets where farmers earn premiums for exceptional work.
takeaways: Specialty coffee scores 80 or above on a 100-point scale
It represents roughly the top 5 to 10 percent of production
Specialty premiums incentivize quality at the farm level

faq.question: How is specialty coffee scored and graded?
faq.answer: Certified Q-graders evaluate coffee using the SCA cupping protocol, scoring attributes like fragrance, flavor, aftertaste, acidity, body, balance, and sweetness on a 100-point scale. Coffee scoring 80 or above is specialty grade. Scores above 90 are considered exceptional.

faq.question: Is specialty coffee worth the higher price?
faq.answer: For those who appreciate nuanced flavors, yes. Specialty coffee offers complexity and transparency that commodity coffee cannot match. The premium also returns more value to farmers. Whether the taste difference justifies the cost is ultimately a personal judgment.
